question: Lynch (2002h) Table 3 (p. 315): which cells are entered now that the PDF is at hand and a row can name its predecessor?
chosen_reading: The cells that were not rows: Mota (all seven columns; nine rows), Loniu *bw, *pw and medial and final *mw, Manam and Dobu *pw > p, Nemi's cross-over reflexes (*bw > ŋg beside mbw, *mw > ŋ beside mw, *pw 'pw?' as disputed), Tongan *bw and *pw > p, Wayan *bw > ŋg and *mw > ŋ. Rows of lects that do not descend directly from POc name POc as predecessor (parent_lect_id poc): Mota (under PNCV), Nemi (under Proto-New Caledonian), Tongan (under Proto-Tongic), Dobu (under Proto-Papuan Tip), Waya (under PCP). Not entered: Lau (Solomons), which is not a lect; Anejom̃, whose cells are the Lynch (2001) rows through Proto-Southern Vanuatu; Pohnpeian (pw beside p for *b, mw beside m for *m), which are the PMc rows 'before round vowels' of Bender et al. (2003a); the PEOc row (*p fortis, *v lenis), since Proto-Eastern Oceanic is an alternative node without rows (the user's decision); Table 4 and the appendix, which are word lists.
alternatives: Enter the Pohnpeian doublets as sporadic rows on Pohnpeian; add Lau (lauu1247) as a lect.
